claims.statement: Elastic documents API keys created in the Elastic Cloud Enterprise UI for authenticating calls to the Elastic Cloud Enterprise RESTful API, as an alternative to bearer tokens obtained with a username and password.

sources.supports: For key-based API authentication, you can create an API key through the Elastic Cloud Enterprise UI. Once created, you can specify the key in the header of your API calls to authenticate.

claims.statement: An Elastic Cloud Enterprise API key has the same permissions as its owner and by default expires three months after creation, configurable to Never.

sources.supports: The API key has the same permissions as the API key owner.; By default, the API key will expire three months after its creation date, but you can set the expiration to Never.

claims.statement: The Elastic Cloud Enterprise page on accessing the ECE API from the command line says to include a generated ECE API key in an HTTP header on API requests and shows it as an Authorization header with the ApiKey scheme (curl -H "Authorization: ApiKey $ECE_API_KEY" against the ECE coordinator API at /api/v1/deployments); the same page shows a temporary bearer token with the Bearer scheme as the separate token-based method.

sources.supports: Once you’ve generated your API key, you need to include it in an HTTP "Authentication" header when making API requests: curl -k -X GET -H "Authorization: ApiKey $ECE_API_KEY" https://$COORDINATOR_HOST:12443/api/v1/deployments
You can also authenticate using a temporary bearer token. ... curl -k -X GET -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://$COORDINATOR_HOST:12443/api/v1/deployments

openQuestions.question: The page read does not state the header scheme or any key grammar; whether the ECE key shares the Cloud API key representation is unresolved.
This candidate is recorded from the claims above only; format, variants, history and benign siblings have not been researched.

The ECE command-line page names the header "Authentication" in prose but writes Authorization in both curl examples; the record follows the example header name and keeps the prose wording as an unresolved discrepancy.

The ECE command-line page says that once set, the API key lasts indefinitely, while the ECE API keys page (claim lifecycle) says the key expires three months after creation by default and can be set to Never; not reconciled here.
The carrier is now documented; the key value grammar (prefix, alphabet, width, encoding) and whether it shares the Cloud API key representation remain undocumented in the pages read.
